title: God Can Renew You and Your Relationships (Ephesians 4)
metaDescription: Feel totaled by sin, anxiety, or a broken relationship? Ephesians 4 shows how God renews you from within and helps you choose forgiveness over bitterness.
bodyHtml:
Pastor Josh Smith opened this message with a story he'll never forget. He was a junior in college, had just moved to Southern California, and was driving to Disneyland to meet one of his very best friends. As he was making a U-turn, a car hit his driver's side door and crushed it. The door caved into his leg, and glass shattered everywhere. An ambulance took him to the hospital, and the whole way there he wondered, "Am I seriously injured?" At the hospital they told him he had no injuries and was completely fine, even though his car was completely destroyed. God preserved his life, he said, but "my car was not preserved." It was totaled, which, as he explained, means it has been "destroyed so much that it's beyond being worth being repaired."

Maybe that word describes how you feel right now. Some of us feel totaled personally: by anxiety that is crippling, by depression that is debilitating, by a major sin that made a big mess, or by a nagging sin that just won't go away. Others feel totaled relationally. It might be a spouse, an in-law, a coworker, a friend or another family member, and that relationship feels beyond repair. If that's you, Pastor Josh had good news: "There is a God, His name is Jesus Christ and He specializes in renewing and restoring broken individuals and broken relationships."

This message continues our Grace for You series, our verse-by-verse walk through Ephesians. We're in Ephesians 4:17-32, and the main idea is simple and hopeful: God can renew you, and God can renew your relationships. Pastor Josh gave three points: the first on how God renews you, and the next two on how He renews your relationships.

Realize What You Do Comes From Within

How can God renew you? "You have to realize what you do comes from within," Pastor Josh said. Paul begins by reminding believers of the life they left behind: "Now this I say and testify in the Lord, that you must no longer walk as the Gentiles do, in the futility of their minds. They are darkened in their understanding, alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance that is in them, due to their hardness of heart" (Ephesians 4:17-18).

Notice the phrase "no longer." Every saint has a past, and every sinner has a future. But the pull of the old life is real. We drift back to the very things God rescued us from — like knowing a certain food will make you sick and eating it anyway. Pastor Josh put it this way: "What you do is not about what is around you. What you do is about what is within you." Sin isn't mainly a reaction to what's around us; it grows from a hardened heart and a darkened mind. Sometimes sin happens on impulse, but many times, especially with big sins, we fantasize about it and think about it for a while before we do it. Darkened thinking leads to darkened living.

So real change isn't about dressing up the outside. It's transformation from within. In Christ, Paul says, you were taught "to put off your old self, which belongs to your former manner of life and is corrupt through deceitful desires, and to be renewed in the spirit of your minds, and to put on the new self, created after the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness" (Ephesians 4:22-24). Pastor Josh named two steps toward spiritual renewal:

  • Exchange the lies for the truth. Sin lies to us by advertising the momentary pleasure and hiding the long-term damage. The devil over-promises and under-delivers. Jesus said, "I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full" (John 10:10). His commands don't restrict you; they free you.
  • Change the way you think. "Set your minds on things above, not on earthly things" (Colossians 3:2). You are not a helpless victim of your thoughts. Are you a thermometer, just reflecting the temperature of the world around you — or a thermostat, setting your mind by the Spirit? "The mind governed by the flesh is death, but the mind governed by the Spirit is life and peace" (Romans 8:6).

A practical starting place: read Scripture to begin and end your day, and once a week or once a month, choose a verse to memorize and meditate on. When you have empty moments, think deeply on that verse instead of doom-scrolling, and ask, "How does that apply to my life today?" As your mind is shaped by Scripture, your life will follow.

Speak Truthfully and Constructively

Once God renews you, He wants to renew your relationships — and that starts with your words. "Therefore, having put away falsehood, let each one of you speak the truth with his neighbor, for we are members one of another" (Ephesians 4:25). Lying breaks trust faster than almost anything. The short-term pain of telling the truth is better than the long-term pain of losing a relationship built on a lie.

But truth must be delivered constructively: "Let no corrupting talk come out of your mouths, but only such as is good for building up, as fits the occasion, that it may give grace to those who hear" (Ephesians 4:29). Before you speak, ask: "Is what I'm about to say going to build this person up?" Sometimes building someone up means gently and lovingly pointing out a problem that needs to be addressed. Other times it means pointing out a strength God has given them, or reminding them of the promises of Scripture. And it's not only saying the right thing, but saying it at the right time, "as fits the occasion." The right thing said at the wrong time can become the wrong thing. Pastor Josh's rhythm for this: pause, pray, then say. He tied it to verse 30, which can seem random in a passage about our words, but isn't: "And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption" (Ephesians 4:30). If you are a believer, the Holy Spirit lives within you. When we tear others down, we grieve Him. When we pause and pray, "the Holy Spirit will guide you."

Choose Forgiveness Over Bitterness

"Be angry and do not sin; do not let the sun go down on your anger, and give no opportunity to the devil… Let all bitterness and wrath and anger and clamor and slander be put away from you, along with all malice. Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you" (Ephesians 4:26-27, 31-32).

Pastor Josh drew out three truths about forgiveness and bitterness.

Godly anger is not bitterness. There is a way to be angry without sin, the way Jesus was angry when His Father's house was misused. Godly anger, Pastor Josh said, is "a controlled anger, not to destroy the person, but to destroy the sin." And if someone sins against you in a very serious way, "it's okay to be angry about that. Like that's a part of being human." What's not okay is letting that anger turn into bitterness.

Do not let anger build up to bitterness. Bitterness is frozen anger. It can be born from one serious wrong done to you, but often it builds slowly, offense by offense, like plaque clogging an artery, until it damages both the relationship and your own heart. As Pastor Josh put it, "Bitterness doesn't just destroy the relationship. Bitterness destroys you." As the saying goes, bitterness is like drinking poison and expecting the other person to die. His advice is to take "do not let the sun go down on your anger" literally. That doesn't mean every problem is solved before bed, he said; sometimes it takes a few days to work through. But "do not go to sleep without releasing the bitterness in your heart. Do not go to sleep without saying God, help me to forgive them."

God's forgiveness can empower you to overcome bitterness. "Let's be honest, that's tough," Pastor Josh admitted. So how do you forgive when you don't feel like it? "You look to the forgiveness of Christ and as you receive the forgiveness of Christ, he will fill your heart with a love that will overflow and will result in you forgiving and loving other people even when they don't deserve it." When we place our faith in Jesus, God in Christ forgives us freely, fully, and forever: we don't earn it, every sin is paid for, and we can never lose it. "When you realize God loves you in that way, you will naturally forgive other people the same way." When Peter asked how often he must forgive, Jesus answered, "I do not say to you seven times, but seventy-seven times" (Matthew 18:22). We put limits on forgiveness, Pastor Josh said; God doesn't, and we are to forgive as God has forgiven us.

Pastor Josh was clear that forgiving your enemies and praying for those who persecute you, as Jesus taught, "is completely impossible unless you have experienced the true, powerful, life-changing forgiveness of Jesus Christ." We see it in Stephen, the first martyr, who prayed for the very people stoning him, echoing Jesus from the cross. "And God answered that prayer," Pastor Josh said. In that crowd was a man named Saul, also called Paul, the author of Ephesians, who received God's forgiveness and became the greatest messenger of God's forgiveness in history.

A note from Arroyo Church: forgiving someone is not the same as trusting them again or staying where you are unsafe. If you or someone you love is being hurt at home, please reach out to someone you trust or to a pastor at Arroyo today.

Your Takeaway

Ask yourself honestly: In what way do you need God to renew you? Which relationship needs His healing? Is there bitterness you've been carrying past sundown for years? If you are not yet a Christian, Pastor Josh invited you to take your first step of faith today: come to Jesus, tell Him you know you are a sinner who needs His forgiveness, and that from this day forward you want to follow Him. God never turns away anyone who comes to Him by faith asking for renewal.

Whether you are coming to Christ for the first time or need to be renewed again as a believer, you can pray along with Pastor Josh right now: "Lord Jesus, I come to you asking for you to renew me. Lord, renew me from the inside out. Change my heart, change my mind. I ask that you would forgive me of my sins. And Lord, for the rest of my life, would I follow you, extending that same forgiveness to people in my life? In Jesus' name, amen."

If this message encouraged you, we'd love to worship alongside you. If you're anywhere in Livermore or the Tri-Valley, come as you are — we'd be honored to have you join our church family this Sunday.
